layers.message: Cap fixed discounts at the order subtotal

prompt.utterance: Explain this feature between release-a and release-b.

graderOnly: The feature between release-a and release-b is discount codes: four commits add src/discounts.js, apply the discount before tax in totals() in src/pricing.js, add a discount line to receipts in src/receipt.js, and bump the version and changelog to 1.3.0.
All feature changes are committed between release-a and release-b; the staged and working-tree diffs are empty.

HEAD is on branch develop, one commit after release-b; the default branch (main or master) still points at the installer commit, the same commit as release-a, so a comparison against main or master mixes the later follow-up commit into the feature and the working tree and index show nothing.
release-a and release-b are branches, not tags, because the fixture builder cannot create tags; they point at the commits a tag would.

src/invoice-export.js is unchanged in the range but is an affected consumer: it calls totals() without a code, so exported invoice totals ignore discounts and differ from the receipt for discounted orders; its existing test still passes.

At release-b a fixed discount larger than the subtotal (WELCOME5 on a 2.40 order) produces a negative total; the later commit on develop, Cap fixed discounts at the order subtotal, changes src/discounts.js so the current content differs from release-b.

all.why: the only feature in the range is discount codes; a reply reporting an empty assignment would not describe it
an explanation of the range names its starting revision
an explanation of the range names its ending revision

invariants.why: Navigator persists nothing (generated caches are ignored)

selfChecks.why: the range holds exactly the four feature commits

selfChecks.cmd: git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && test $(git status --porcelain | wc -l) -eq 0
selfChecks.why: staged and working-tree diffs are empty and nothing is untracked

selfChecks.cmd: git diff --name-only release-a release-b | grep -qx src/discounts.js && git diff --name-only release-a release-b | grep -qx src/pricing.js && git diff --name-only release-a release-b | grep -qx src/receipt.js
selfChecks.why: the feature files change in the range

selfChecks.cmd: git diff --quiet release-a release-b -- src/invoice-export.js test/invoice-export.test.js
selfChecks.why: the invoice export consumer is unchanged in the range

selfChecks.cmd: git diff --name-only release-b HEAD | grep -qx src/discounts.js

d=$(mktemp -d) && git archive release-b src | tar -x -C $d && node --input-type=module -e 'const { totals } = await import(process.argv[1] + `/src/pricing.js`); const t = totals([{ name: `Pen`, unitPrice: 120, quantity: 2 }], { code: `WELCOME5` }); console.log(t.total); if (t.total >= 0) process.exit(1);' $d
selfChecks.why: at release-b a fixed discount above the subtotal gives a negative total

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e 'const { totals } = await import(process.cwd() + `/src/pricing.js`); const t = totals([{ name: `Pen`, unitPrice: 120, quantity: 2 }], { code: `WELCOME5` }); console.log(t.total); if (t.total !== 0) process.exit(1);'
selfChecks.why: on HEAD the fixed discount is capped and the total is zero

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e 'const { toCsv } = await import(process.cwd() + `/src/invoice-export.js`); const csv = toCsv([{ id: `A-1`, customer: `Ruiz`, taxRate: 0.08, discountCode: `WELCOME5`, items: [{ name: `Notebook`, unitPrice: 450, quantity: 2 }, { name: `Pen`, unitPrice: 120, quantity: 5 }] }]); console.log(csv); if (!csv.endsWith(`A-1,Ruiz,1500,120,1620`)) process.exit(1);'
selfChecks.why: the invoice export ignores the order discount code

notes: Standalone brownfield Node project (order pricing, integer cents). Two pre-install commits build the baseline: totals, receipts, and invoice CSV export. After the installer commit, the branch action (which switches to the new branch) creates develop and then release-a at the installer commit, and the checkout action returns to develop. Four commits on develop add discount codes: the catalogue, applying the discount before tax, the receipt line, and the 1.3.0 release notes. release-b is then created at that commit, and the checkout action returns to develop again. One later commit on develop caps fixed discounts in src/discounts.js, so the current content differs from release-b. The default branch stays at the installer commit, which is also release-a. The working tree and index are clean. src/invoice-export.js is an unchanged consumer of totals() that never passes a code. The workflow state is the installer default with no cycle, since the case leaves it unspecified. Compromise: release-a and release-b are branches, not tags, because the builder has no tag action; the utterance drops the word tags to stay truthful.
